title: Concept-coordinate meta-learning with held-out factor combinations
hypothesis: A support-set encoder that emits two factor-specific Mirror coordinates generalizes to held-out joint concept combinations, achieving query NRMSE within 1.10x additive task-vector composition and lower actual serialized N=20 payload bytes than an unstructured LEO latent encoder.
physical_object: shared conditional linear model and shared concept decoder
mirror_coordinate: two support-inferred factor coordinates, one per concept axis
logical_multiplicity: held-out combinations of independently observed concepts
controls: direct additive task-vector composition from single-factor interventions
LEO unstructured 2D latent decoded through calibrated basis with gradient adaptation
factorized Mirror coordinates inferred from held-out support via least squares
full-space support least squares upper control

development.selection_metric: LEO query NRMSE on held-out joint composition; select gradient step size only

success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror query NRMSE <=1.10x direct task-vector composition and actual N=20 serialized bytes lower than LEO; both factor interventions recovered independently.
failure_gate: Any quality/bytes/identifiability gate miss, or additive task vectors match Mirror at equal/fewer bytes.
boundaries: Synthetic aligned linear concept test only.
Do not treat combination count as independent capacity.
No natural concept, language, or nonlinear task claim.

amendments.reason: To make factor identifiability testable without leaking held-out combinations, each world provides paid single-factor intervention examples that recover the shared decoder; the held-out joint task is inferred only from its own support set. This is a mechanism-level concept-coordinate screen, not full neural MAML/LEO reproduction. Controls are direct additive task-vector composition, gradient-adapted LEO latent, and full-space support least squares.
